text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - The Slovak government is expected to discuss a package of unspecified measures designed to overcome current economic "discrepancies" at its regular session next week, Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik said.
- The finance ministry is considering cutting some five billion crowns from budget expenditures to concrete projects.
- The government plans a 10 percent increase in energy prices for corporate customers.
- The European Investment Bank is expected to extend a one billion crown loan and the Industrial Bank of Japan should provide a four billion crown credit to help finance motorway construction.

- The main opposition parties have agreed to accept the next invitation to round table discusions by Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar to help implement recommendations on improving democratic principles which were made by the EU-Slovak joint parliamentary committee.
- The National Property Fund (NPF), the state privatisation agency, on Monday approved the sale of 15 percent in oil refiner Slovnaft a.s.

- Parliament starts its regular June session on Tuesday. The preliminary agenda has 46 items, including a draft law on returning the right to decide on direct privatisation sales from the NPF back to the government.
- Volkswagen's Bratislava plant plans to complete 60,000 cars in 1998, up from the planned output of 38,000 this year.
- The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) on Monday set the lower limit on bids at its it repo tender at 8.8 percent, the equivalent of the discount rate.
- The NBS on Monday approved a measure tightening banks' liquidity rules. The new measure requires banks to cover liabilites of up to one months maturity with assets of an equal duration.
- The trade deficit totalled 29.9 billion crowns for the first five months of the year, according to preliminary figures from the Finance Ministry.
- The government is expected to discuss measures aimed at boosting Slovakia's capital investment abroad at its regular sessdison on Tuesday.
SME - Jan Slota, chairman of the ultra-right minor coalition party, the Slovak National Party (SNS), said the ruling coalition was not in danger of disintegrating.
PRAVDA - The Finance Ministry said the full year budget deficit without the debt servicing should not exceed 11.7 billion crowns.
- Foreign Minister Zdenka Kramplova said there was some room to intensify discussions with the European Union and NATO.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The Slovak banking sector is not expected to meet its minimum reserve requirements at the end of the month.
